_status: Module 4, Lesson 4.1 'Phones and tablets' and 'Office devices or personal ones?' (learner guide of 21 October 2026), including NPC Circular 2023-06 on known, properly configured devices. Cases invented around the fictional RSSO cast.

options.label: IT wipes the work profile only

items.text: Sol's office-issued phone is left on a jeepney. She reports it within the hour.

facts.v: The office controls it: full baseline; lost or stolen, IT locks and wipes it

items.reason: Reporting at once is what makes the remote wipe possible.

items.text: Ben's personal phone, with a separate work profile under the office's policy, is stolen.

facts.v: A written policy, an approved-apps list and a separate work profile; IT wipes the work profile only

items.reason: App management (MAM) protects only the work apps on a personal phone.

items.text: A staff member roots his phone to install a game, then signs in to work email on it.

facts.v: Never root or jailbreak a device used for work: it removes the phone's own protections

items.reason: A rooted phone cannot be trusted with office data.

items.text: Dan opens applicant records at home on a laptop of his own that IT has never set up.

facts.v: Only known devices, properly configured to the office's security standards, may access personal data

items.reason: An unknown device has an unknown baseline: no proof of updates, protection or encryption.
